# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Brandon Still

## 1. Executive Summary & Risk Profile
- **Participant Name:** Brandon Lee Still
- **Risk Assessment Level:** High Risk (LSCMI Score: 141)
- **Primary Criminogenic Drivers:** Antisocial Pattern (reactive hostility/impulsivity), Education/Employment deficits, Companions (criminal network vs. single anticriminal peer).
- **Current Placement:** Transitional Federal Halfway House (Columbia, SC).
- **Supervision Status:** 5 Years Federal Supervised Release.

## 2. Clinical & Facilitation Interventions
### Modeling Neutrality & Managing Resistance (Standards 1.5 & 3.2)
- **Antisocial / Defensive Statements:** When Brandon discusses 'setting the tone' or acting tough with strangers, avoid arguing or direct confrontation. Use neutral curiosity: *'How does setting the tone that way affect your federal probation status if someone escalates?'*
- **Minimization & Excuses:** Acknowledge his feelings of frustration neutrally. Re-center every conversation on his self-interest: earning early discharge from supervision, earning steady income, and keeping his freedom.
- **Prosocial Lever:** Actively integrate his positive relationship with his best friend (who achieved $180k legal income after incarceration) into goal-setting sessions as concrete proof of legal success.

## 3. Stability & Health Action Plan
- **ADHD Non-Stimulant Management:** Schedule an evaluation with Cooperative Health for alternative non-stimulant ADHD medication to address daytime sleepiness and focus deficits without violating federal halfway house rules.
- **Physical Outlet Integration:** Support and protect his daily structured gym/weightlifting schedule to manage restlessness and emotional stress.
- **Vocational Readiness:** Focus placement on structured, fast-paced 1st-shift physical roles (e.g., concrete, manufacturing, distribution) that keep him engaged and minimize unstructured down-time.

## 4. Case Management Goals & Milestones
1. **Week 1:** Complete medical intake at Cooperative Health for non-stimulant ADHD treatment.
2. **Week 2:** Submit applications to 3 fair-chance employers with 1st shift schedules.
3. **Week 3:** Attend interview skills coaching focusing on non-defensive communication.
4. **Week 4:** Secure full-time employment and establish a daily structured routine.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Brandon Still

## Welcome to Your Next Chapter
Brandon, you have already shown incredible resilience by keeping clean for over 5.5 years and maintaining a strong vision for your future. Your dedication to your physical fitness and your goal of building a lucrative, legal career—just like your friend who successfully transitioned—is your blueprint for success. This guide is designed to help you hit your goals, stay focused, and maintain full control over your future.

---

## Key Community Resources

### 1. Medical & ADHD Support (Non-Stimulant Evaluation)
- **Cooperative Health (Eau Claire Health Center)**
  - **Services:** Sliding-scale primary care and behavioral health evaluation for non-stimulant focus support.
  - **Phone:** (803) 786-4831
  - **Address:** 4605 Monticello Rd, Columbia, SC 29203
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://cooperativehealth.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=4605+Monticello+Rd,+Columbia,+SC+29203)
  - **Next Step:** Call to set up a primary care intake and request a non-stimulant ADHD assessment.

### 2. Free Maintenance Prescriptions
- **Welvista Headquarters**
  - **Services:** Prescription assistance program for chronic condition management.
  - **Phone:** (803) 933-9183
  - **Address:** 2700 Middleburg Dr, Suite 105, Columbia, SC 29204
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://welvista.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2700+Middleburg+Dr,+Suite+105,+Columbia,+SC+29204)
  - **Next Step:** Submit application through case manager once prescriptions are issued.

### 3. Community & Re-entry Support
- **Midlands Fatherhood Coalition**
  - **Services:** Re-entry support, court navigation, and peer support groups.
  - **Phone:** (803) 933-0530
  - **Address:** 1821 Hampton St, Columbia, SC 29201
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://midlandsfathers.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=1821+Hampton+St,+Columbia,+SC+29201)
  - **Next Step:** Contact intake for orientation on peer support networks.

---

## Target Employment Opportunities

### 1. Midlands Concrete & Paving Solutions
- **Role:** Concrete Finisher Helper / General Laborer
- **Pay & Shift:** $18.00 – $23.00 / hr | Day Shift (7:00 AM – 3:30 PM)
- **Why It Fits:** Active, physical work that utilizes your strength and keeps you moving throughout the day on a predictable 1st-shift schedule.
- **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=concrete+paving+laborer&l=Columbia%2C+SC)

### 2. CMC Steel South Carolina
- **Role:** Mill Operator Trainee / Material Handler
- **Pay & Shift:** $19.00 – $24.50 / hr | Day Shift (7:00 AM – 3:30 PM)
- **Why It Fits:** High-paying, structured industrial environment with growth potential and full safety gear provided.
- **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.cmc.com/en-us/careers)

### 3. Palmetto State Distribution Center
- **Role:** Order Selector / Package Handler
- **Pay & Shift:** $17.50 – $21.50 / hr | 1st Shift (7:00 AM – 3:30 PM)
- **Why It Fits:** Fast-paced warehouse setting with direct weekly pay and consistent hours.
- **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=warehouse+order+selector&l=West+Columbia%2C+SC)

---

## Your 4-Week Action Checklist

- [ ] **Week 1:** Complete medical consultation at Cooperative Health for non-stimulant focus medication.
- [ ] **Week 2:** Complete application and phone screen for Midlands Concrete or CMC Steel.
- [ ] **Week 3:** Practice communication strategies with your Navigator to handle workplace stress calmly.
- [ ] **Week 4:** Start full-time 1st-shift employment and set up a savings plan for post-halfway house living.

assessmentData.interviewTranscript:
ASE MANAGEMENT BRIEF
Participant: Brandon Lee Still
Date Completed: August 6, 2026
Prepared by: Intake Specialist / Center Director
1. RISK PROFILE
● Risk Level: High [141]
● Primary Domains:
○ Antisocial Pattern (Main Driver overridden by LSCMI Supplemental) [10]
○ Companions (Secondary Driver overridden by LSCMI Supplemental) [10]
○ Education/Employment (High-scoring LSCMI Domain) [143]
● Domain Indicators:
○ Antisocial Pattern: History of reactive hostility, impulsivity, poor self-management,
physical altercations (including a fight while in federal prison), and an intimidating
style with strangers to enforce physical boundaries [9, 114, 116].
○ Companions: High density of criminal acquaintances and friends, with very few
anticriminal supports in his active social network [99, 191].
○ Education/Employment: Chronic vocational instability (only two jobs in his life, both in
his 20s), multi-year gaps of unemployment, and high school incomplete (with a
history of disciplinary suspensions) [91, 93, 161].
2. BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS
● Typical Triggers:
○ Interpersonal Disrespect: Perceived disrespectful behavior or challenging actions
from strangers in the community [114]. Brandon explains that he "sets the tone" and
lets people know he "ain't going to play" to avoid being "run over" like other guys
coming out of prison [114, 115].
○ Emotional Sadness / Isolation: Situational stress or emotional lows where he tends to
isolate, withdraw from communication ("gets in his feelings" and refuses to answer
his phone), and avoid support networks [122].
● Escalation Tendencies:
○ Physical Force / Defensive Hostility: Under perceived disrespect or threat, he tends
to "set the tone" and establish boundaries aggressively, which historically led to
fights, including a physical altercation while in federal prison [114, 116].
○ Hostile Outbursts: Hostility and impulsive expressions are prominent when he feels
others are trying to exploit or disrespect him [9, 114].
● Decision-Making Patterns:

-- 1 of 5 --

○ Impulsive / Acting Before Thinking: Highly impulsive with clear problem-solving and
self-management skill deficits; has an increased tendency to act before thinking [9,
113].
○ Criminogenic Financial Resolution: Historically resolved financial and drug-seeking
needs by engaging in drug trafficking (distribution of methamphetamine and heroin)
to fund his daily habit, rather than pursuing legal, stable employment [102, 105].
● Authority Response Style:
○ Polite Compliance with Undercurrent of Denial: Brandon generally presents as polite,
cooperative, and superficially charming with program staff and supervisors,
expressing a strong desire to comply with supervision and complete it early [9, 108].
He completed RDAP and has no disciplinary reports in prison [89, 108].
○ Denial & Minimization Barrier: However, he exhibits significant responsivity barriers
related to denial and minimization; he frequently makes excuses for his behavior and
blames others for his present difficulties [5, 6].
● Substance Relapse Patterns:
○ Self-Medication for untreated ADHD: Historically dependent on heroin and marijuana,
using daily depending on the year [102]. While he has been clean for 5.5 years, his
substance use was deeply tied to self-medication for untreated childhood ADHD,
boredom, and a lack of structured daily routine [105, 109]. Future relapse risk is
highly correlated with unstructured free time, peer pressure, or untreated ADHD
symptoms [99, 105, 110].
3. PATTERN OVER TIME
● Age at First Justice Involvement:
○ First arrested at age 18 [88, 89]. (Note: Intelius records a drug possession charge
filed in Aiken, SC, in May 2014 [16, 17]. Under his stated DOB of 1999, he would
have been 15; under his Intelius DOB of 1989, he would have been 25. He reports
his first arrest was "like 18" [88].)
● Number/Frequency of Incarcerations:
○ This is his first incarceration sentence [87].
○ His current federal sentence of 120 months (10 years) for conspiracy to distribute
methamphetamine and heroin resulted in serving approximately 6 years in custody
before his transitional release to a halfway house [1, 88, 89].
● Recidivism Timing Patterns:
○ Brandon completed his previous state-level First Offender Act probation successfully
[89, 90]. However, he was actively engaging in the federal drug conspiracy while on
state probation, indicating a pattern of continued criminal involvement hidden under
superficial compliance [90].
● Escalation or Stability Trends:
○ His criminal trajectory escalated from local possession and trafficking charges (which
were dismissed under the state First Offender Act) to a major federal conspiracy
charge involving high-volume meth and heroin distribution [88, 102]. This represents
an escalation in both criminal sophistication and legal consequences [88].
● Supervision Violation History:

-- 2 of 5 --

○ No official technical supervision violations or revocations on record; his state
probation was completed successfully [89, 90].
4. ACUTE / EMERGENCY NEEDS
No acute needs identified at intake. [37]
5. STRUCTURAL STABILITY FACTORS
● Housing Stability Level: Stable. He is currently residing in a transitional federal halfway
house which he finds decent and liveable [121]. This placement allows him to reside
rent-free and save money [111].
● Driver’s License Status: Satisfactory. He has a valid driver's license, regular State ID, Social
Security card, and birth certificate [87].
● Education Credential Status: Completed. Finished 10th grade in academic high school and
subsequently completed an online GED through Christian Kingdom Academy, which was
officially recognized and registered by the BOP [91, 92].
● Recent Substance Use: Abstinent. Clean from all illicit substances for approximately 5.5
years, having maintained sobriety since his first six months of federal incarceration [103].
● Employment History Pattern: Highly Unstable. Brandon has only held two jobs in his entire
life (both in his 20s) and has experienced severe multi-year gaps of unemployment, including
a continuous three-year period of unemployment immediately preceding his arrest [90, 91].
He lacks vocational training or a trade, which presents a major barrier to long-term financial
independence [105].
● Supervision Intensity: High. Undergoing 5 years of federal supervised release following his
transition out of the halfway house, requiring strict compliance, employment, and regular
drug testing [1, 108].
6. LEGAL & PLACEMENT CONSTRAINTS
● Pending Charges: None [118].
● Court Obligations: Sentenced to a $100.00 special assessment in his federal judgment [1].
● Supervision Restrictions:
○ Subject to standard federal supervision travel and association restrictions [108].
○ ADHD Medication Restriction: A critical constraint exists where Federal Supervision
(FS) does not allow him to take Adderall (his preferred and historically effective
childhood ADHD medication) while residing at the halfway house [110]. He is forced
to wait until he transitions to standard probation to resume it, causing significant
daytime sleepiness and requiring him to coordinate with mental health staff for
alternative, non-stimulant medications [110].
● Sex Offender Registry Requirement: No [117].

-- 3 of 5 --

● Movement/Contact Restrictions: Halfway house curfew, sign-out logs, and programmatic
requirements [121].
7. RESPONSIVITY & ENGAGEMENT PROFILE
● Literacy Limitations: None identified; average literacy. Completed 10th grade and has a GED
[91, 92].
● Cognitive Considerations:
○ Low Verbal/Learning Intelligence: Reports significant learning difficulties during
school [7, 79]. He may struggle with highly abstract or heavily text-based
programming, requiring practical, concrete, and highly structured
cognitive-behavioral interventions [245].
● Trauma Reactivity:
○ Grief & Loss: Severe family-related trauma and grief. He has lost three brothers (two
to drug overdoses, one to gun violence) [97].
○ Childhood Domestic Violence: He witnessed severe domestic violence (parents
fighting) during childhood, which likely contributes to his hyper-vigilance and reactive
boundary-setting [124].
● Authority Sensitivity:
○ Defensive Boundary-Setting: While polite and cooperative, Brandon is highly
sensitive to perceived disrespectful treatment or feeling that others are trying to "run
over" him, which can trigger defensive hostility [114].
○ Excuses and Blame: He frequently engages in denial and minimization, making
excuses and blaming others for his present difficulties [5, 6].
● Motivation Style:
○ High Motivation for Legitimate Success: Highly motivated to stay out of prison,
maintain employment, pass drug tests, and earn early termination from supervision
[108].
○ Prosocial Peer Influence: His primary motivation is reinforced by his best friend, who
successfully turned his life around after serving a 10-year prison sentence and made
$180,000 legally in his first year doing roofing adjustments [100]. This relationship is
a critical prosocial lever that should be utilized in case planning to demonstrate that
legal financial success is achievable [102].
● Learning Preferences / ADHD Accommodations:
○ Untreated ADHD Accommodation: Brandon has an active childhood diagnosis of
ADHD [109]. Currently untreated with stimulants due to federal supervision rules
[110], he suffers from severe daytime sleepiness, lack of focus, and restlessness
[110, 122].
○ Structured, Active Modules: He learns best through hands-on, active, and brief
educational modules. Long, unstructured lectures will fail.
○ Physical Outlet Integration: Staff should actively support his daily weightlifting routine
at the gym, which serves as his primary physical outlet for stress and energy
management [98, 115].

-- 4 of 5 --

○ Calm, Coaching Style: Case managers should use a calm, firm, coaching style that
avoids direct power struggles, respects his boundaries, and focuses on concrete,
legal financial goal-setting [27, 100].

-- 5 of 5 --
